ozonation.definition:
n. The act of treating with ozone; also, the act of
   converting into, or producing, ozone; ozonization.
ozonation.translation: [化] 臭氧化; 臭氧化作用

ozonator.translation:
[化] 臭氧化发生器
[医] 臭氧发生器

ozone.definition: n. a colorless gas (O3) soluble in alkalis and cold water; a strong oxidizing agent; can be produced by electric discharge in oxygen or by the action of ultraviolet radiation on oxygen in the stratosphere (where it acts as a screen for ultraviolet radiation)
ozone.translation:
n. 新鲜的空气, 臭氧, 使人愉快的影响

ozone-ether.translation: [医] 臭氧乙醚(乙醚、过氧化氢、醇合剂)

ozoner.translation: n. 可驾车进入的剧场

ozonic.definition: a. Pertaining to, resembling, or containing, ozone.
ozonic.translation: a. 臭氧的, 臭氧般的, 含臭氧的

ozonide.definition: n any of a class of unstable chemical compounds resulting from the addition of ozone to a double bond in an unsaturated compound

ozoniferous.translation: a. 含臭氧的, 产生臭氧的

ozonium.translation:
n. 束丝菌属
[网络] 菌丝束

ozonized.translation: v. 以臭氧处理, 使含臭氧, 变成臭氧( ozonize的过去式和过去分词 )

ozonizer.definition:
n. An apparatus or agent for the production or application
   of ozone.
ozonizer.translation:
n. 臭氧发生器
[化] 臭氧化发生器

ozonometer.definition:
n. An instrument for ascertaining the amount of ozone in
   the atmosphere, or in any gaseous mixture.
ozonometer.translation: n. (用以测定空气等中的臭氧含量的)臭氧计

ozonometry.definition:
n. The measurement or determination of the quantity of
   ozone.

ozonophore.translation: [医] 原浆粒(细胞的), 红细胞

ozonoscope.definition:
n. An apparatus employed to indicate the presence, or the
   amount, of ozone.
ozonoscope.translation:
[化] 臭氧检验器
[医] 臭氧检验器

ozonosphere.definition: n a layer in the stratosphere (at approximately 20 miles) that contains a concentration of ozone sufficient to block most ultraviolet radiation from the sun
ozonosphere.translation:
n. 臭氧层
[化] 臭氧层

ozonous.definition:
a. Pertaining to or containing, ozone.
   P () the sixteenth letter of the English alphabet, is a nonvocal
   consonant whose form and value come from the Latin, into which language
   the letter was brought, through the ancient Greek, from the Phoenician,
   its probable origin being Egyptian. Etymologically P is most closely
   related to b, f, and v; as hobble, hopple; father, paternal; recipient,
   receive. See B, F, and M.
